title: Resilience, Peace and Security
gist: Landing/index page for the World Economic Forum's 'Resilience, Peace and Security' story hub (1,648 stories), listing only headlines from Sept–Nov 2026; no article bodies. The headlines signal WEF's editorial focus on cyber resilience, space as a strategic chokepoint, climate-hazard governance, insurance-led resilience, Europe's defence supply chains and energy-system resilience (Ukraine, Gulf/US-Iran conflict).

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum's resilience hub is foregrounding cyber resilience as a leadership agenda for 2027, alongside pieces on how organizations can collaborate on cyber resilience.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Supports continued board-level attention and budget for cybersecurity into 2027; watch cyber-security vendors and cyber insurance.
insights.quote: Cyber resilience in 2027: What leaders need to know

insights.claim: A World Economic Forum article raises the question of whether the next strategic chokepoints could be in space, framing orbital assets as a potential geopolitical vulnerability.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Space infrastructure may be increasingly treated as security-critical; watch space/defence spending narratives.
insights.quote: Could the next strategic chokepoints be in space?
insights.locator: Could the next strategic chokepoints be in space? (Article, 19 November 2026)

insights.claim: A World Economic Forum headline argues that Europe's defence readiness depends on building more resilient industrial supply chains.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: European defence build-out implies investment in the industrial supply base, not just prime contractors.
insights.quote: Why Europe’s defence readiness depends on building more resilient industrial supply chains
insights.locator: Why Europe’s defence readiness depends (Article, 27 October 2026)

insights.claim: World Economic Forum headlines claim Gulf countries' decades-long focus on resilience paid off during the US-Iran conflict, and that Ukraine's energy system offers resilience lessons for the world.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Energy/infrastructure resilience under conflict is a live theme; the page references a US-Iran conflict as context.
insights.quote: Gulf countries have focused on resilience for decades. Here's how it paid off during the US-Iran conflict
insights.locator: Gulf countries have focused on resilience (Article, 3 November 2026)

insights.claim: A World Economic Forum piece argues that avoiding the next energy crisis requires a systems approach to resilience, with a related piece on measuring the energy, food and water nexus.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Energy security framed as cross-sector (energy-food-water) systems risk rather than a single-commodity issue.
insights.quote: Rethinking resilience: Avoiding the next energy crisis requires a systems approach

insights.claim: A World Economic Forum article contends that climate hazards are inevitable but catastrophes are a failure of governance.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Shifts climate-loss attribution toward policy/adaptation failure; relevant to adaptation and resilience spending.
insights.quote: Climate hazards are inevitable. Yet catastrophes are a failure of governance

insights.claim: World Economic Forum headlines position insurance as a tool for building a more resilient economy and urge businesses to improve insurability and investability through place-based resilience.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Insurability is being framed as a gating factor for investment in climate-exposed locations; watch insurers and resilience infrastructure.
insights.quote: Why businesses should improve insurability and investability through place-based resilience
insights.locator: Why businesses should improve insurability (Article, 12 November 2026)
